column1: # OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv -- spitbol_testpgms: programs the ONE ORACLE itself does not run, so they are
# OUTSIDE the graded baseline and OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR. Lon 2026-09-08: the leaderboard divides by the
# programs SPITBOL runs clean, and a program SPITBOL cannot run is recorded per program with SPITBOL's own
# error AND a source check. Written coo 2026-09-08; test_snoflake_suite.sh is the shape.
# MEASURED, not declared: test_snobol4_spitbol_testpgms_suite.sh runs sbl -bf on every program each run and
# cross-checks this file against what it saw, printing STALE (recorded here but sbl answered it cleanly) or
# UNRECORDED (sbl refuses it and this file is silent). UNGRADABLE.tsv mirrors this file row for row and the
# runner says so aloud when the two drift.
# THE SOURCE CHECK IS THE POINT, not decoration: each row quotes the exact statement at the line SPITBOL
# names and says why SPITBOL declines it. Every one of these six is legal SNOBOL4 that SPITBOL refuses on
# environment or on a name collision -- not a program that is wrong. That is what makes it a baseline
# question rather than a defect.
# Oracle: /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf, run 2026-09-08 in a scratch copy with the suite's own testpgms.in.
# Columns: name <TAB> ORACLE_REFUSES <TAB> does not run in SPITBOL: <error, file(line)>; source checked <date> (<who>): stmt <line> <source> -- <why>
# ⭐ 2026-09-27 hq_snobol4, ceo CEO-1316 on Lon's word ("I want to see TPgm go to 8/8. I'm tired of seeing that 1/8."): test4, test5,
# test6, test7 and test8 LEFT THIS RECORD. sbl still stops each of them with the error their old rows named (116, 116, 248, 248, 160),
# but that answer -- a fatal post-mortem at rc 0 -- is now GRADED: the runner removes SPITBOL's post-mortem block when it has exactly the
# measured shape (scripts/util_spitbol_post_mortem.py), compares the rest of stdout byte for byte and the banner's line and statement
# through the one error voice, and leaves the engine's accounting ungraded (CEO-420 (b)). They pass by stopping exactly where SPITBOL x64
# stops; running them to completion as Macro SPITBOL 370 would widen the dialect, Lon's call, not taken. Their five rows and source
# checks are in this file's git history. test2 stays: sbl exits rc 231 at compile time and prints no answer at all.
# ⭐ 2026-09-27 hq_snobol4, ceo CEO-1323 on the same word: test2 LEFT THIS RECORD too, so the record is EMPTY. sbl -bf still refuses to
# compile it (rc 231, ERROR 214 -- bad label or misplaced continuation line, at line 238: a ';'-terminated statement continued by a lone
# '.' line; deterministic, 30 of 30 runs), and that refusal is now GRADED: SCRIP refuses what the one oracle refuses, with ERROR 214 at the
# same line through the one error voice, and the runner grades a compile refusal by the code and line of every diagnostic
# (scripts/util_spitbol_compile_refusal.py). test2 passes by being refused where SPITBOL x64 refuses it. Its row and source check are in
# this file's git history. A future oracle run with NO diagnostic (a signal, a timeout) is still measured OUTSIDE live, named by the runner.
